data.why: The repo's own gulp fetch_data task downloads a sample dataset (healthy.zip) into data/healthy, which webpack-dev-server serves at its root (mapped via the DATA_DIR='./healthy' DefinePlugin constant) and db_summary.json inside it marks a default subject/trial, so the UI's folder-icon dataset picker lists it with no manual uploads needed.

goals: Load a shoulder-motion trial (torso/scapula/humerus pose trajectory) and visually inspect the 3D kinematic reconstruction
Compare joint angle/orientation plots against the animated 3D bone models frame-by-frame
Scrub through an activity's time samples to spot anomalous orientations or discontinuities in the trajectory
Switch between subjects/activities in the sample dataset to compare kinematic patterns
Bring in a custom dataset (own STL bone models, landmark CSVs, and pose trajectory CSV) via manual file selection to analyze patient-specific data

review.summary: The tree gets the point right: comparing how different conventions split humerus and scapula orientation into sub-rotations, frame by frame. It covers every section of the in-app help, and the 12 cited screens I opened all match their nodes. Before filing it needs fixes: one overclaiming phase, a cross-trial phase that never compares anything, two oversized features (f2, f6), and check.json screen references that point to the wrong images.
